title: Envelope
description:
Every ordinary structured result. `T` is the per-primitive `data` payload; errors
use [`ErrorData`]. Field order is the spec example's order.

data.description: Per-primitive payload; never contains private keys or reusable secrets.

next.description:
Machine next action, or `null` when nothing is expected of the caller.
Always emitted, `null` when absent (required-nullable in the schema:
`NextAction | null`).

operation_id.description: Present for effectful or long-running work; absent for pure reads.

schema_version.description: Major schema version of this document.

state.description: Operation state; synchronous reads report `succeeded` or `failed`.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal findings. Always emitted (listed in the schema's `required`); a
lenient reader still accepts omission as empty.

AccountName.description: Remote account name on a destination.

Certainty.description: Whether a statically evaluated value is decided.

ClockMeasurement.description:
A destination clock measurement (ADR-0008 D5 §6.5 item 4): the destination's
clock lags local time by at most `behind_upper_ms`.

behind_upper_ms.description: Upper bound of the destination clock's lag, in milliseconds.

rtt_ms.description: Round trip of the measurement, in milliseconds.

Code.description: Stable semantic code (ADR-0006 §5). Readers treat an unlisted value as an error with exit 1.

ConfigProvenance.description: Where a configuration directive was read: a display path and a 1-based line.

path_display.description: Display path (`~` for the home directory; `--redact` aware).

wording.description: The exact D8 disclosure sentence(s): human text, not a code.

ConsumerExecutable.description: A client executable an integration relies on.

version.description: Reported version, when a local query ran.

ConsumerIntegration.description: How a consumer reaches the binding (no secrets).

environment.description: Environment variables a launcher should set (names and values; never secrets).

executables.description: Client executables the integration relies on (R-SS-03).

overrides.description: Consumer settings another source keeps in force.

pairs.description: One entry per destination/account pair of the grant (ADR-0007 §7).

signing_endpoint.description: Signing endpoint path or pipe name, if one is materialized.

ssh_config_include.description: Generated OpenSSH include path, if one is materialized.

ConsumerOverride.description:
A consumer setting another source keeps in force (ADR-0007 §8 "Git under
`run`"). Names the setting, never its value.

CredentialAvailability.description:
Credential availability (spec §4.3): how long new authentications keep working
without further action.

oneOf.description: Usable now; no claim about later.
Depends on a refresh before the deadline.
A human step may be needed for new authentications.
Not established (the default for older documents).

Cursor.description: Opaque, reader-scoped resumption token. Never parse it outside the runtime.

DeclarationRef.description:
The declaration a fresh eligibility relied on (ADR-0007 §7 "Launch eligibility is
checked fresh"). The CLI's pre-launch check requires the same revision and
endpoint and an unexpired `expires_at`.

DestinationClock.description:
A pair's destination clock (ADR-0008 D7 item 3). Wire forms:
`{"measured":{…}}` or `"unmeasured"`. Per pair the weakest is shown.

DestinationScopeEnforcement.description: Destination-scope enforcement levels (spec §4.3), ordered weakest to strongest.

oneOf.description: Client configuration routes to the destination.
Agent restriction authenticated to the destination (spec S03).
Server-side principal mapping verified by test.
A separately tested isolated execution boundary.

EndpointKind.description: The transport of an agent endpoint.

EndpointRef.description:
A reference to an agent endpoint. The locator is a path or pipe name, never a
secret; it is compared exactly (a changed locator lapses a declaration,
ADR-0007 §7).

Enforcement.description:
Structured guarantee report (spec §4.3, §11.3 `enforcement`). Every claim
references evidence held by the runtime; `Unknown` is a valid value.

identity_selection.description:
⟨M03⟩ How identities are selected (§5 item 8). Omitted when absent, so every
M01/M02 report (and every grant record that stores one) is unchanged; reads
`unknown` when absent ([`Self::identity_selection`]).

new_authentication_expiry.description: What stops new authentication at expiry.

new_signing_expiry.description: ⟨M03⟩ What stops new signatures at expiry (claim-gated); `unknown` when absent.

connection_policy.description: ⟨M03⟩ The effective connection policy and its wording.

consumer.description:
Consumer integration descriptor; contains endpoints and config references,
never secrets.

credential_availability.description:
Credential availability (spec §4.3), computed fresh for every result. Always
written; a document that omits it reads as `unknown`.

environment_id.description: Environment the binding is pinned to.

lock_continuity.description:
⟨M03⟩ Lock continuity (§5 item 7). Omitted when absent, so every M02 result
is unchanged; reads `not_verified` when absent ([`Self::lock_continuity`]).

offline_until.description: Usable with no controller/issuer contact until.

provider.description: The provider's observed state, for existing-access mechanisms.

EvidenceBasis.description:
How a reported fact was established (ADR-0007 §7). `declared` is an owner
statement, never an observation.

oneOf.description: Declared by the owner through an attended decision.

EvidenceEntry.description: One piece of evidence behind a reported value (§5 item 7).

EvidenceSource.description: Where an evidence entry comes from.

oneOf.description: This pair's own runtime verification (ADR-0008 §17.1 item 13).

ExistingConnectionsMode.description:
What happens to owned dedicated connections at the admission deadline (ADR-0008
D8 item 1). `strict` is narrowing; `graceful` (the default) is widening.

oneOf.description: Existing dedicated sessions may stay connected (spec §6.6 default).
Owned connections are closed at the deadline.

ExistingConnectionsPolicy.description: Effect on existing connections at expiry (spec §6.6).

oneOf.description: Dedicated connections may stay; owned masters are closed.
Owned connections are closed at expiry.

⟨M03⟩ A `run` of a program other than the verified `ssh`: its connections
are not owned, so nothing closes them (ADR-0008 D8 item 2).
Global file (`~/.gitconfig` or the XDG file).

IdentitiesOnly.description: `IdentitiesOnly` as statically evaluated for the alias.

IdentityBacking.description:
What backs an identity entry (ADR-0007 §7, F9): an agent when the private key
file is absent, a file when it is present (stat only; never opened).

oneOf.description: Private key file absent: used through the alias's agent.

IdentityEntry.description: One entry of an alias's identity list.

cleared.description:
Whether a fallback clearance (ADR-0007 §7, M2-R05) cleared it; present only
where a clearance was evaluated (readiness, the pre-launch check, doctor).

fingerprint.description: Public fingerprint (`SHA256:…`) read from the `.pub` file, when present.

provenance.description: Directive location, when it comes from a file.

IdentityEntryKind.description: The kind of an identity-list entry.

IdentityEntrySource.description: Where an identity-list entry comes from.

IdentityId.description:
Adopted existing-access identity in the catalog (ADR-0007 §7; m02-plan §5
item 1). Runtime-generated at adoption; never derived from key material.

IdentitySelection.description: Whether ssh can only use the adopted identity for an alias (ADR-0007 §3 item 3).

oneOf.description: Only the adopted identity can be offered.
Other identities the configuration adds can be offered.
Static evaluation cannot decide (for example behind `Match exec`).
Exclusive client configuration plus signer filtering (runtime evidence).

IdentitySelectionReport.description: The static identity selection of an alias (ADR-0007 §3 item 3).

entries.description: Every entry ssh may try, in order.

InteractionKind.description: The human step an authentication may need (ADR-0007 §7 interaction profile).

oneOf.description: No interaction (only ever `declared` for a native agent key).
Not known; never satisfies a non-interactive requirement.
The issuer is a same-user child process.

LockContinuityReport.description:
Whether credentials survive a desktop lock (`lock_continuity`; R-UX-03). Reads
`not_verified` when absent: only a claim-table entry makes it `verified`.

oneOf.description: A verified claim-table entry covers this platform and store.

MultiplexingMode.description:
Owned multiplex masters (ADR-0008 D8 item 3). `disabled` is the default and
narrowing; `owned_masters` is widening.

oneOf.description: The supervisor runs one owned master per pair slot.

NewAuthenticationExpiry.description: What ends new authentication at expiry (spec §4.3 "Expiry").

oneOf.description: Certificate validity and the signer both stop.
Nothing stops new authentication (existing fixed credentials).
The signer stops signing at the deadline.

NextAction.description:
Machine next action (spec §11.2 `next`, §11.6 "machine-readable next action").
`action` names are stable; parameters are present only when relevant.

action.description: Stable action name; defaults come from [`Code::default_next_action`].

cursor.description: Cursor to resume from after a resync.

decision_ref.description: Nonsecret reference to a pending owner decision.

provider_interaction.description:
The provider-owned interaction, with action `interact`, for
`PROVIDER_LOCKED` and provider-owned `INTERACTION_REQUIRED` (ADR-0007 §7).
Never combined with `decision_ref`: provider dialogs are not Heimdall
decisions (spec §5.5).

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested minimum delay before a retry.

NoninteractiveEligibility.description: Whether a pair may be used on the no-interaction path, computed fresh per result.

reason.description: Why not, when not: one of [`noninteractive_reason`]'s values.

OperationState.description: Operation states (spec §11.4). A caller timeout is not a state change.

oneOf.description: Accepted and journaled; not yet running.
Waiting for an owner or provider decision on an owner channel.
Settled: failed with a classified error.

Settled: explicitly cancelled; the result says whether an irreversible or
uncertain step may have occurred.

Unresolved: an external effect may or may not have applied. Quiescent until
reconciliation settles it to `succeeded` or `failed`; never purged while
unresolved; never retried blindly.

OverrideSource.description: Where an overriding consumer setting comes from (tagged by `kind`).

oneOf.description:
An OpenSSH configuration directive (for example an effective
`IdentityAgent`).
Owned masters are closed at the deadline (claim-gated).

PairIntegration.description:
One destination/account pair's integration (ADR-0007 §7). `endpoint`, `alias`,
`mechanism`, `identity_selection` and `selection_observed_at` are history
(prepared facts); the interaction and eligibility fields are computed fresh in
the transaction that builds each result (M2-R04).

declaration.description: The live declaration the eligibility relied on.

declared_at.description: When the owner declared it (`basis: declared` only).

identity_selection_report.description:
⟨M02⟩ The full static identity selection behind `identity_selection`: its
entries (each alternative's `cleared` filled by the one clearance rule) and
`IdentitiesOnly` (ADR-0007 §12.14 item 6, §12.15 item 3(c)). History, like the
verdict: the runtime stores it in the prepared facts. Serde default, omitted
when absent, so an older document decodes with `None`; a missing report never
clears a fallback (ADR-0007 §7).

ProbeLevel.description: The probe ladder levels (ADR-0007 §6; spec §10.2), weakest first.

oneOf.description: Parse and evaluate without executing anything (the default).
TCP connect and read the identification line.
Host-key verification with nothing to sign (needs `--allow-config-commands`).

ProviderAvailability.description: Whether the provider can sign now (ADR-0007 §7 "Provider states").

ProviderInteractionRef.description:
The provider-owned interaction a next action points at (spec §5.5). Used with
action `interact` for `PROVIDER_LOCKED` and provider-owned
`INTERACTION_REQUIRED`; never combined with `decision_ref`.

provider.description: The provider whose dialog it is.

ProviderKind.description: Which provider serves an agent endpoint (ADR-0007 §7 "Detection is passive").

oneOf.description: An OpenSSH-compatible agent (`ssh-agent`, the Windows OpenSSH agent service).

Not determinable passively (for example the Windows `openssh-ssh-agent` pipe,
F18).

observed_at.description: When it was observed (RFC 3339, explicit offset).

observed_level.description: The probe level that observed it.

ReadinessCondition.description: A condition the result's readiness depends on (§5 item 7; F03, F14).

oneOf.description: The in-process signer must be running.
After a reboot an attended time confirmation is needed.
The issuer store must be unlocked at start (macOS keychain).
Only a signer restart (the K_env is lost) needs a re-issue.
Remote processes are never claimed to stop (ADR-0008 D8 item 5).

RemoteRevocation.description:
The remote part of revocation (`revocation.remote`), gated by the claim table
exactly like `enforcement.revocation`: `unknown` until a claim exists (F11).

oneOf.description: Bounded by the issued certificates' expiry.
Trust may remain until the registry line is removed.
No bound is known (a key-only restore, ADR-0008 D4 item 4).

destination_clock.description: The weakest destination clock of the grant's pairs.

latest_possible_credential_expiry.description: Latest instant an issued credential could be accepted; absent = unknown.

oneOf.description: Bounded only by an already-issued credential's expiry.

SchemaVersion.description: A `schema_version` value as received from a peer.

oneOf.description: Connections Heimdall did not start are not controlled.

Warning.description: A non-fatal finding attached to a result.

message.description: Human text; may change without breaking callers.

oneOf.description: Shared OS-user environment; same-user convenience only.
